model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route, net debt zero)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' 31 (NA.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:15147). Already expensed inside non-interest expenses, so it sits inside the pre-tax margin; sbc_pct_path is 0 to avoid charging it twice.
inputs.share_count_basis: 383.581M common shares at 2026-07-31 (Q3 FY2026 press release) grossed up 1.2% for dilution (Q3 basic/diluted EPS 3.29/3.25) = 388.3M fully diluted. Held FLAT: NCIB buybacks (391.1M -> 383.6M over 9 months) are a use of the FCFE being valued, so shrinking the count as well would double-count them.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.75% in CAD: 10y GoC ~3.3% + beta ~1.1 x ERP ~5.5% + ~0.4% for Quebec concentration and Capital Markets trading share of revenue. Same level as BMO/TD (9.75%), between RY (9.5%) and BNS (10.0%). Held at 9.75% in all three scenarios so risk is charged once, in the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 lease costs are inside non-interest expenses (pre-tax margin); no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is nil (FY2025 0). Preferred shares and LRCN/AT1 distributions (FY2025 165, NA.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:14702) removed INSIDE the flow as a pre-tax-equivalent 1.4pp of revenue (165 / (1 - 23.5%) = 216 on 15,551), so preferred capital is NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the same route as BMO, RY, TD and BNS.TO, so the Canadian banks stay comparable. Deposits are operating funding: net_debt = total_debt = cash = 0. Engine mapping: 'ebitda_margin' = ADJUSTED pre-tax income after provisions for credit losses, less the pre-tax equivalent of preferred/LRCN distributions; SBC and D&A = 0 (already in non-interest expenses); 'capex' = equity retained to keep CET1 at a 13.25% run-rate as the balance sheet grows = (TCE/revenue 1.68) x g/(1+g). TCE/revenue: common equity 31,460 less goodwill 3,101 and intangibles 1,748 (FY2025) = 26.6bn on TTM revenue 15,551 = 1.71 at the 13.5% CET1 reported at Q3 FY2026, scaled to 13.25% = 1.68. FY0 anchors: TTM revenue 15,551 (Q4 FY25 3,698 + 9M FY26 11,853); TTM ADJUSTED pre-tax 6,733 (FY25 5,836 - 9M FY25 4,331 + 9M FY26 5,228) = 43.3% margin, less 1.4pp preferred = 41.9%. Adjusted (not reported) because the excluded items are CWB/LBC integration charges (finite, ~C$250m pre-tax/yr, ending FY2027) and non-cash CWB intangible amortisation. TTM adjusted diluted EPS 12.70 (11.28 - 8.46 + 9.88); reported TTM NI 4,854. last_fcf = TTM adjusted NI to common ~4,971 less retention at 6% growth (1,479) = 3,492 FCFE; reported_fcf holds reported TTM NI to common (4,854 - 165) for audit, there is no bank 'FCF' line. Laurentian retail/SME portfolio purchase (~C$4.1bn loans, close ~Nov 2026) is included in year-1 growth; its capital cost is assumed met from the ~25bp CET1 headroom above 13.25%, so that headroom is NOT credited in an equity bridge.
inputs.historical_growth_note: Revenue/equity CAGRs inflated by the all-share CWB acquisition (Feb 2025, +~50M shares).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management medium-term adjusted diluted EPS growth objective 5-10% (midpoint); equity CAGR rejected because CWB was paid for in stock
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 17.9% vs reported EPS 3yr CAGR 1.6% and 5yr 12.1%: equity growth is inflated by the ~C$5bn all-share CWB acquisition (FY2025) and reported FY2025 EPS is depressed by CWB integration charges and initial PCL on acquired loans. Neither is a clean organic growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Periods: FY2020-FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022-FY2025 (3yr), October year-end. FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF dominated by deposit and trading-book flows). Adjusted diluted EPS FY2024 10.39 -> FY2025 11.28 (+8.6%) -> TTM 12.70.

base.margin_rationale: Year 1 drops 0.9pp from the 41.9% TTM as Capital Markets trading (Q3 revenue +34% YoY) normalises and PCL drifts from ~0.30% to ~0.35% of loans; CWB cost synergies and LBC scale recover part of it. Consistent with adjusted ROE ~16.5-17% (17%+ target by 2027).
base.capex_rationale: Retention = 1.68 x g/(1+g): equity needed to keep CET1 at 13.25% as revenue (and RWA) grows.

bull.margin_rationale: Capital Markets holds most of its 2026 run-rate, CWB revenue synergies and Laurentian cross-sell land, credit stays benign; adjusted ROE ~18%.

bear.margin_rationale: Quebec/Canadian housing and tariff-driven credit cycle lifts PCL to ~0.60% of loans in years 1-2 while trading revenue mean-reverts; margins recover only partly as CWB/LBC integration costs bite. Adjusted ROE ~13-14%.

scenario_narratives.base: NBC digests CWB and the Laurentian retail/SME book on schedule: revenue grows ~6% for two years (organic loan growth ~5%, LBC adds ~1pp) and then slides toward nominal GDP, Capital Markets gives back part of its exceptional 2026 trading run, and PCL settles at ~35bp. Adjusted ROE holds ~16.5-17%, payout plus buybacks run ~70% of earnings, and the bank compounds as a high-return, Quebec-anchored franchise with a national footprint, not a re-rating story.
scenario_narratives.bull: The CWB deal proves to be a genuine pan-Canadian platform: Western Canada commercial cross-sell and the Calgary/Edmonton capital-markets build add revenue synergies on top of cost synergies, the fee-heavy Wealth and Capital Markets franchises keep outgrowing the balance sheet, credit stays benign, and management beats its 17%+ ROE target. Revenue compounds 7-9% for three years and margins widen ~1.5pp.
scenario_narratives.bear: A tariff-driven Canadian slowdown hits Quebec housing and the commercial book acquired with CWB: PCL roughly doubles to ~60bp for two years, trading revenue mean-reverts hard from 2026 highs, and two concurrent integrations bring client attrition and cost overruns. Revenue stalls, margins fall ~5pp before partly recovering, and ROE sits near 13-14% - still profitable and well-capitalised (CET1 13.5%), so this is an earnings bear, not a solvency bear.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): late-cycle Canadian credit with tariff uncertainty, record trading revenue that tends to mean-revert, and two integrations at once. Base 50%: guidance and Q3 FY2026 run-rate support it. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs synergies, trading strength and benign credit to all hold together. Same 25/50/25 as BMO, keeping the Canadian banks comparable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the equity cash it can distribute after holding the capital its growth needs, discounted at the cost of equity. Deposits are funding, not debt, so there is no net-debt bridge. The question is whether NBC's premium P/B (~2.4x book, ~16x TTM adjusted EPS) is earned by its best-in-class ROE.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital Markets revenue (~26% of the mix, Q3 FY2026 +34% YoY) is at a cyclical high; the base already trims it, the bear removes it
Quebec housing concentration plus the CWB commercial book in a tariff-hit economy: PCL is the largest swing factor in the flow
CET1 run-rate: a regulator- or market-driven move to 13.5-14% raises retention and cuts FCFE ~3-5%
Cost of equity: +/-50bp moves the base value roughly -/+10%
Laurentian retail/SME close (targeted Nov 2026) and CWB AIRB model transition deferred to FY2027 (RWA relief timing)
